  "abstract": "Background: The integration of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems into power grids presents challenges due to the intermittent nature of solar irradiance. Accurate solar power forecasting is critical for grid stability, energy trading, and operational planning. Machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) have emerged as dominant approaches for PV power prediction, but the literature lacks a structured synthesis of methods, performance, and gaps. Objective: This systematic literature review (SLR) aims to synthesize ML/DL-based solar PV power forecasting studies from 2021–2025, identify best-performing models, evaluate common datasets and metrics, and highlight research gaps. Method: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, 87 studies were retrieved from Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and ScienceDirect. After duplication removal (n=12), title/abstract screening (n=75 screened; 43 excluded), and full-text eligibility assessment (n=32 assessed; 14 excluded), 18 studies were included for final synthesis. Results: Hybrid models (CNN-LSTM, Transformer-based) consistently outperform standalone ML models. RMSE and MAE are the dominant evaluation metrics. Public datasets (NREL, DKASC) are underutilized compared to proprietary data. Conclusion: Key gaps include limited generalization across geographic regions, lack of uncertainty quantification, and insufficient multi-horizon benchmark studies. Future work should prioritize transfer learning and probabilistic forecasting.",
